question.problem: The function $f(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x-1}{k})$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{3}^{x+2}}{5}+\frac{1}{5}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x-1}{k})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5y-1}{k}).\end{aligned}
$$

We make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5y-1}{k}) \\ {3}^{{log}_{3}⁡((5y-1)/k)} & ={3}^{x} \\ \frac{5y-1}{k} & ={3}^{x} \\ 5y-1 & ={3}^{x}\cdot k \\ 5y & ={3}^{x}\cdot k+1 \\ y & =\frac{{3}^{x}\cdot k}{5}+\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{3}^{x}\cdot k}{5}+\frac{1}{5}.$ 

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k={3}^{2}=9.$
